prompt: Use $api-design-engineering to design a notes API for a small same-origin web app. One Python monolith, SQLite, existing cookie sessions and CSRF middleware, about 80 users. Existing endpoints use camelCase JSON and {items, nextCursor} lists. Need create, edit and list my notes; no sharing or third-party access. Give the concrete contract and implementation outline, with the decisions that matter.
rubric: Uses existing monolith/sessions and camelCase; no unjustified OAuth/gateway/service/queue
Concrete CRUD contract, own-note access, input limits and existing CSRF reuse
Bounded lists and explicit edit/failure behavior; assumptions distinguished

prompt: Fix the invoice-edit API in this fixture. Users report that knowing an invoice ID can let them edit someone else's invoice, protected fields can change, and two editors using the same ETag can both overwrite each other. Preserve existing title-edit clients and response conventions. Implement the smallest safe fix and focused tests; do not add dependencies. Follow PROJECT.md.
rubric: Scopes tenant and owner/admin access with no unauthorized side effects
Only title writable; unknown fields stay ignored, protected fields unchanged, input validation preserved
Strong optional If-Match compares atomically; one winner under concurrent same-version edits; legacy omission still works
Existing envelopes and valid edit behavior retained; no unrelated infrastructure

prompt: Use $api-design-engineering to stabilize the reservation API in this disposable fixture. After response loss clients retry; two application processes can receive the same request concurrently. Customers see duplicate reservations and negative stock. Keep the existing function signature and response envelope. Implement a focused fix using the existing SQLite store, and add meaningful regression tests. Follow PROJECT.md.
rubric: Atomically persists deduplication and mutation; works across database connections/processes
Same key same payload replays; different payload rejects; scopes keys to tenant/operation
Atomic stock invariant and no effects after insufficient stock/invalid input
Lost response and concurrency tested; no new service/dependency/global config

prompt: Review this proposed release for a public API used by mobile versions we cannot force-upgrade and generated Java/Kotlin clients. GET /orders currently returns a bare array of all orders, sorted by createdAt. Proposal: same path will return {items,nextCursor}, default to 100 records, sort by updatedAt, and add a new value 'paused' to the status enum. Existing errors are {code,message}. We also want Problem Details and OpenAPI 3.2.1, but the generator only accepts 3.0.3. Recommend a safe practical release approach.
rubric: Recognizes envelope/truncation/sort/error and enum consumer compatibility
Preserves legacy behavior during explicit migration or opt-in; no silent truncation
Toolchain support governs OAS upgrade; no blindly mandatory new spec/version convention
Concrete coexistence/usage/retirement/recovery evidence

prompt: Review a multi-tenant GraphQL API. node(id) checks a logged-in user but looks up by global ID. A process-global DataLoader caches customer objects by customer ID, including fields filtered for the first caller. Admin fields are hidden from the normal UI. The HTTP gateway allows 60 requests/minute; each query may use arbitrary aliases and unbounded nested lists. Proposal: disable introspection to solve data leaks and overload. Give prioritized corrections while keeping developer clients usable.
rubric: Object/function/field authorization independent of UI and introspection
Identity/tenant-safe cache and node lookup; no global permission-sensitive cache reuse
Cost/breadth/alias/list/concurrency controls, rate limit alone insufficient
No unjustified GraphQL rewrite or blanket introspection cure

prompt: We operate Go and Java gRPC services and a REST gateway with generated mobile clients. An inventory mutation has no explicit deadline. App code retries DEADLINE_EXCEEDED three times; the service mesh also retries. The team says the first request was cancelled so it cannot have committed. A proto change reuses removed field 7 for a new string; it compiles, so they call it backward compatible, including the REST JSON output. Review the release and suggest a proportionate repair.
rubric: Timeout/cancel ambiguous for committed mutation; safe identity/reconciliation required
Explicit deadlines/propagation and coordinated bounded retries
No field-number reuse; reserve old names/numbers; wire/source/JSON compatibility differentiated
Focused changes with actual language/runtime checks

prompt: Review our payment webhook handler design. It JSON-parses the request, reserializes it, then verifies HMAC. It uses payload.metadata.tenantId to select an account, returns 200, and starts an in-memory task to credit the wallet. A dedup dictionary is local to each worker and is written after crediting. Events with timestamps <= lastTimestamp are ignored. Customers can also configure an HTTPS delivery URL for outgoing notifications; redirects are followed automatically. Explain the actual failure cases and a practical correction.
rubric: Exact raw-byte/provider signature validation and verified account mapping
Durable acceptance; atomic dedup/effect; unordered/distinct event handling without timestamp-only loss
Lost ack/worker crash and outgoing retry/replay ownership addressed
SSRF includes redirects/DNS/address boundaries, no blanket URL regex cure

prompt: An existing REST endpoint GET /reports/{id} authenticates and checks report ownership in the DB, then returns appCache[reportId] if present. On a miss, it computes a response filtered by the caller's role and caches it. Responses include Cache-Control: public,max-age=600. Tenant-scoped IDs may overlap. A CDN uses the URL as its cache key. Under load, p95 grows and the handler performs one detail query per line item. A proposed fix adds Vary: Authorization and Redis. Diagnose and choose the smallest safe improvement.
rubric: Recognizes application and CDN isolation independently; Vary does not fix app cache
Permission-filtered role/principal/tenant data and revocation/freshness handled safely
Measures/fixes N+1/query/payload bottleneck before speculative Redis
No security-breaking stale fallback; verification covers cross-tenant cache hits

prompt: We are extending a SaaS export API in an existing PostgreSQL app with an existing worker. POST /exports writes an export row, commits, publishes a queue message, and returns 202. Sometimes publish fails after commit. The worker writes a result URL into the row; GET /exports/{id} only checks that someone is logged in. The download URL never expires. Export authorization calls an internal service; the proposed outage fallback is to allow the request. Design a focused reliability/security repair and the verification needed.
rubric: Durable accepted work and dual-write recovery using existing store/worker
Tenant/owner authorization of submit/poll/download and scoped expiring access
Fail-closed authorization outage with useful explicit failure; legitimate export workflow retained
Worker retry/dedup/recovery/observable states with proportional scope
